source: LLM-Trader coding agent (external evidence, not authority over this repository)
fingerprint_verification_note: The descriptor lives in LLM-Trader (contracts/adaptive-ecology-v1.json). Slime's pin discipline requires recomputing the descriptor hash from its own content and comparing to the declared and pinned values; that check is an admission precondition and cannot be performed from this repository.
ordered_feature_names_note: Two literal names contain spaces ('sentiment_strongly bullish', 'sentiment_strongly bearish'). The ordered names are part of the fingerprint; exact strings matter.
normalization_semantics: unit-invariant decision values/flags/one-hots; the three intermediates are percentile ranks (CDF, ties included) in [0,1] against the frozen basis
normalization_set_note: The handoff does not enumerate which three names are the percentile-rank intermediates; the refusal condition on normalization needs the exact set.
normalization_basis_semantics: fit_context_basis on the hashsplit's train side only; the basis hash rides the export manifest; held-out/live values never move a feature
causal_boundary: observations carry only decision-boundary information (the bar's decision decomposition and card snapshot); outcomes are separate later records; evaluation labels are never input
episode_identity: episode_id = instrument|decision_ts|context_hash|horizon - several candidates (models, seeds, the deterministic baseline) share it; candidate ranking groups by it
outcome_join: the outcome record's sample_id equals the observation's; comparable_outcome is the repository's canonical definition (realized/capital, else counterfactual/qty)
join_key_note: sample_identity names the identity proposal_id; outcome_join and the consumer brief use sample_id. Either an alias must be declared or the field defined.
logging_policy_semantics: the logged action distribution (propensity) recorded at the decision; null when the source stated none
evaluation_only_fields: the evaluation record type (world, planted, labels) - never model input
surrogate_worlds_verified: regime_transition (labels joined per sample; the other mechanisms are that world's nulls - None); the registry holds nine deterministic worlds via research/validation/surrogates.py
baseline_consumers: the LinUCB bandit (reuses the same primitive)
the deterministic baseline candidate rows (the same-episode bar)
commands_run: scripts/guard.ps1 (exit 0); the fixture generation; the focused tests; the full suite
known_limitations: the 2-D views are not persisted (absent, not fabricated)
the capture-on-surrogate-world path does not exist yet (the evaluation join is verified with fixture rows on the world timeline)
the manifest's module_file_hash changes with code edits (consumers pin the fingerprint, not the file hash)
open_questions: whether the consumer wants categorical/action as side metadata (v1) or in the vector
recommended_slime_representation: consume the 15-d vector per sample as a frozen reference space plus the delayed outcomes as supervision and the evaluation labels as a separate ground-truth stream; never recompute features; keep its own latent state/archive
recommended_slime_first_experiment: regime_transition with its null channels - detection delay and null false-positive rate against the persistence baseline and the logistic selector, then volatility_jump and liquidity_shock
slime_must_not_assume: that it may recompute or re-derive features

trader_answers.source: LLM-Trader agent, verified against the pinned descriptor, landed in docs/04 section 7 (commit 85f8a08)
trader_answers.join_key: alias, not a second field: the wire field on all three record types is sample_id (string), whose value IS the domain's proposal_id = episode_id|model|attempt, with episode_id = instrument|ts|context_hash|horizon. Join is exact string equality outcome.sample_id == observation.sample_id (evaluation likewise); grouping uses episode_id; both ids are opaque and must never be parsed.
trader_answers.feature_names: literal, spaces included: sentiment_strongly bullish and sentiment_strongly bearish are literal feature_names members (positions 13 and 14 of 15), built as 'sentiment_' + value over ('bullish','bearish','strongly bullish','strongly bearish','neutral'); match byte-for-byte.
trader_answers.normalization: the three percentile-rank features are volatility_rank, cycle_period_rank, inst_freq_rank (intermediates ranked against the frozen train basis, ties included, side='right'; a missing intermediate becomes the 0.0 neutral fill). There is no normalization enum on the wire: acceptance is feature_view == 'context_vector/v1' plus the exact fingerprint. A machine enum would be a descriptor addition requiring a fingerprint bump and a deliberate re-pin.
trader_answers.evaluation_record: world (str), planted (dict; raw hidden-state arrays excluded), and labels (dict[str, Optional[bool]] keyed regime_transition, volatility_jump, liquidity_shock; null = that world's null channel) are fields of the evaluation record, alongside type, sample_id, and episode_id.
trader_answers.fingerprint_recipe: sha256(json.dumps(descriptor, sort_keys=True).encode('utf-8')).hexdigest(), lowercase hex; Python canonical JSON: object keys sorted, default separators, ensure_ascii=True, no trailing newline. The descriptor is the manifest's descriptor object, equivalently contracts/adaptive-ecology-v1.json minus its fingerprint key; do not hash the manifest file bytes. It covers feature_names order (arrays are order-significant) and the normalization semantics via the fingerprinted feature_view and normalization strings, plus record_fields, record_types, major, version, compatibility, and outcome_vocabulary. Reference: runtime/ecology.py::verify_contract.
trader_answers.manifest: fields: contract, fingerprint, descriptor, basis_hash, record_counts, producer{entrypoint, module_file_hash}. basis_hash = first 16 hex of sha256 over the three ranked columns' sorted train breakpoints (canonical JSON). Under the pin only the descriptor is pinned; producer.module_file_hash is provenance and a producer source edit must not force a re-pin; basis_hash and record_counts are data identity. The descriptor has no administrative section: every descriptor edit is an ABI change.
trader_answers.negative_fixtures: observation_with_outcome -> loud (extra field forbidden); observation_nonfinite -> loud; descriptor_wrong_major -> loud; descriptor_reordered_features -> loud (declared != computed != pin); corrupt_torn_tail -> tolerated (killed final append; complete records returned); corrupt_interior -> loud (corrupt JSON). The descriptor and record negatives are invalid by design under the pin; the positive canonical stream plus manifest is the pinned-valid reference.
trader_answers.cadence_and_horizons: neither exists in v1: no cadence field; the outcome record carries a per-row horizon (int). Any change to feature_names, normalization semantics, or record fields moves the descriptor; breaking changes bump the major; additive ones still move the fingerprint, so a deliberate re-pin is required either way.
trader_answers.frozen_sentinel_replay: deterministic under (rows, split, producer): records sort by sample_id, the basis freezes on the split's train side, no wall-clock is added, and evaluation labels are a pure function of the surrogate world plus timeline; witnessed by byte-identical regeneration of the canonical fixture and row-order invariance. Limitations: the manifest carries only basis_hash, not the basis values (verify/compare, not reconstruct); evaluation replay needs the same surrogate world (producer-side).
trader_answers.consumer_checks: wrong-major -> verify_contract; reordered -> fingerprint; missing -> required-field validation; non-finite -> validators with allow_nan=False; observation-with-outcome -> extra='forbid'; features are never recomputed; labels are metadata; no feedback path in v1.
